summary: @servicetitan/marketing-widgets preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares `scripts.preinstall`: `node setup.mjs`. `setup.mjs` is variable-name-obfuscated (systematic `_0xNNNNNN` identifiers, per-callsite indirection wrappers such as `_0x2c3338.OIvQl(dl,...)` hiding `fs`, `https`, `os`, download and exec references) and at install time downloads the Bun v1.3.13 runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v...`, extracts and chmods the binary in a temp directory, and invokes it via `execFileSync(<bun>, [<math_init.js>], {stdio:'inherit'})`. The `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball is a 727 KB single-line `// @bun @bun-cjs` blob with a shuffled string-array decoder (`WV8StW` shifts, `hc1jfK9` decoder against a custom charset). Fetching an alien language runtime at preinstall solely to execute a bundled obfuscated payload bypasses Node/npm-based inspection and runs opaque author-controlled code with the installer's privileges on every `npm install`. The published package name `@servicetitan/marketing-widgets` diverges from the referenced repository `github.com/servicetitan/marketing-integration-widgets`, consistent with a hijacked or squatted release in the ServiceTitan npm scope rather than a legitimate ServiceTitan publication.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
